by: Eric S. Téllez

This tutorial walks through the embedded API end to end: creating a dense (vector)
project and a text project, inserting items, searching, soft-deleting, calibrating for a
target recall, and closing/reopening a project in a later session.

## Installation

`SimilaritySearchEngine.jl` isn't registered yet — develop it from a local checkout (or a
git URL) alongside its own dependencies:

```julia
using Pkg
Pkg.develop(path="path/to/SimilaritySearchEngine.jl")
```

## A dense (vector) project

`create_project` makes a brand-new project directly on disk, at `<workdir>/<dataset>`. By
default it builds a `SearchGraph` (an approximate, self-tuning index) autotuning toward
`minrecall=0.9`:

```julia
using SimilaritySearchEngine
using SimilaritySearch: SearchGraph

workdir = mktempdir()
h = create_project(workdir, "images"; index_type=SearchGraph, minrecall=0.9)
```

Items are appended as a `Vector` of dicts, each carrying a `"vector"` key plus any
metadata fields you want to keep alongside it:

```julia
for i in 1:1000
    append_items!(h, [Dict("vector" => rand(Float32, 32), "label" => "item-$i")])
end
```

(`append_items!` accepts a batch — passing many items in one call amortizes better than
one `append_items!` call per item, though both work.)

Searching returns a `Vector` of `(id, doc_id, distance, deleted)` named tuples, hydrated
with each hit's original metadata id:

```julia
query = rand(Float32, 32)
results = search(h, query; k=5)
for r in results
    println(r.id, " => distance ", r.distance)
end
```

Pass a `filter` predicate — a plain `record -> Bool` function over each candidate's
`Schema.MetadataRecord` — to restrict results without building a separate query language:

```julia
using SimilaritySearchEngine: Schema

recent = search(h, query; k=5, filter = record -> Schema.get_field(record, "label") !== nothing)
```

### Soft deletes

`delete_item!` marks a document as logically deleted; the index itself is untouched:

```julia
delete_item!(h, 1)  # doc_id, not the "label" metadata value

results = search(h, query; k=5)
first(results).deleted  # true if doc_id 1 made the top-5 candidates
```

A soft-deleted candidate is *reported*, not hidden and backfilled — if you need `k` live
results after filtering out deletions, overfetch and page yourself, or let
`SimilaritySearchServer`'s cursor layer do it for you.

### Calibrating for a target recall

`calibrate!` runs a real hyperparameter search and persists the result, so a later
`search(...; minrecall=0.95)` call can serve that target recall from a tuned `BeamSearch`
instead of the constructor's default:

```julia
calibrate!(h; levels=[0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 0.97])
precise = search(h, query; k=5, minrecall=0.95)
```

### Closing and reopening

```julia
close_project!(h)

h2 = open_project(workdir, "images")
same_query_results = search(h2, query; k=5)
close_project!(h2)
```

Every insertion was already persisted incrementally as it happened (see
[Architecture](../architecture.qmd)), so `close_project!` only needs to flush anything
still pending for index kinds that don't persist incrementally on their own.

## A text project

Text projects work the same way, just with a `"text"` key instead of `"vector"`, and
`ftsearch` instead of `search`. `BM25InvertedFile` scores via BM25 over raw
bags-of-words; `InvertedFile` (a weighted, cosine-by-default inverted index) is the other
option:

```julia
using TextSearch: BM25InvertedFile

ht = create_project(workdir, "articles"; index_type=BM25InvertedFile)

append_items!(ht, [
    Dict("text" => "similarity search over dense vectors"),
    Dict("text" => "full text search with an inverted index"),
    Dict("text" => "approximate nearest neighbors in high dimensions"),
])

hits = ftsearch(ht, "nearest neighbor search"; k=3)
for r in hits
    println(r.id, " => distance ", r.distance)
end

close_project!(ht)
```

The vocabulary is trained once, from the *first* batch of text a project receives — tokens
never seen at training time are out-of-vocabulary on every later append (a
`TextSearch.jl` limitation, not a bug in this package), so make sure that first batch is
representative.

## Metadata lookups

`fetch_items` and `exists` accept either the internal integer `doc_id` or the original
`"id"` you supplied when appending:

```julia
fetch_items(h2, [1, 2, 3])
exists(h2, [1, "some-external-id"])
```

## All-pairs nearest neighbors

For a dense project, `allknn` runs `SimilaritySearch.jl`'s batch all-nearest-neighbors
synchronously, in-process (no job queue) — useful for small-to-medium projects where you
want every item's own top-`k` neighbors at once:

```julia
neighbors = allknn(h2; k=10)
first(neighbors)  # (id=1, neighbors=[...], dists=[...])
```
